:::{#thm-kl-divergence-nonnegative}
#### The divergence is nonnegative

Let $p$ and $q$ be [probability mass functions](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf) on the values $x_1, x_2, \ldots$,
with $q(x) > 0$ wherever $p(x) > 0$,
and suppose that

$$\sum_x p(x) \, \bigl\lvert \log_2 \bigl( p(x) / q(x) \bigr) \bigr\rvert < \infty.$$

Then the [Kullback--Leibler divergence](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-kl-divergence),
with base-2 [logarithms](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm),
satisfies

$$\kldivf{p}{q} \ge 0,$$

with $\kldivf{p}{q} = 0$ exactly when $q = p$.

:::

::: {.proof}

Every [sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-summation) here runs over the values $x$ with $p(x) > 0$.
For every $t > 0$, $\ln t \le t - 1$, with equality exactly when $t = 1$.
Apply this with $t = q(x) / p(x)$, and multiply by $p(x) > 0$:

$$
p(x) \ln \frac{q(x)}{p(x)} \le q(x) - p(x),
$$

with equality exactly when $q(x) = p(x)$.
Both sides are summable over $x$.
The left side does by the assumption in the statement,
and the right side does
because $\sum_x p(x) = 1$ and $\sum_x q(x) \le 1$.
So the relation holds for the totals over $x$:

$$
\sum_x p(x) \ln \frac{q(x)}{p(x)}
\le \sum_x q(x) - 1
\le 0.
$$

The left side is $-\ln 2 \cdot \kldivf{p}{q}$,
because the divergence uses base-2 [logarithms](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm),
so $\kldivf{p}{q} \ge 0$.

If $\kldivf{p}{q} = 0$, both relations hold with equality.
The first forces $q(x) = p(x)$ at every $x$ with $p(x) > 0$.
The second then gives $\sum_x q(x) = 1$,
so $q$ has no mass where $p$ has none, and $q = p$.
Conversely, $q = p$ gives $\log_2 (p(x)/q(x)) = 0$ for every $x$.

:::
